The great thing about Google ads is you can be found for anything. However, the downside is that can include services that you don’t actually offer, which Google makes you pay through the nose for anyway. That can end up costing you an absolute fortune, and it’s often almost all completely wasted. Which makes it massively important that you send people through to pages relevant to the keywords you’re bidding on.
 
It’s quite common that when we take over our customers’ Google Ads accounts their keywords aren’t bundled correctly so the ads aren’t specific enough. Or they’re pointing all their ads to the homepage, which is simply not going to be a great landing page for every keyword bundle you use.
 
Being as relevant as possible may seem like common sense, but the number of examples we’ve seen where businesses don’t do this, and the considerable money you can waste on it, make it one of our top Adwords tips to improve your campaigns. Being candid, it’s also one of the very first things we check on day one whenever we take over a new Adwords account.

For all your marketing needs please give us a call so that we can take you and your business to the next level.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMqecaKvP9jwttP-hoR7pCZlFb9wAYku6eoxPM=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2022-10-13T12:00:57", "expires_at": "2023-04-14T12:00:57", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3566637384459306965", "text": "Any business today needs targeted visibility on Google. Most businesses know that this requires optimizing their website and Google Ads, but what most don’t know is that there is a third entity that also needs optimizing: their Google business listing. Officially known as your Business Profile, this powerful listing is a dynamic snapshot of your business that highlights your best features and enables potential customers to quickly find, learn about, and engage with you—all from the SERP. The best part? It’s completely free.

And yet, despite the 167 billion searches performed on Google each month, a BrightLocal study showed that the typical Business Profile only averages 1,260 views during that same period (that’s 0.00000075%!). Even worse, only 59 actions are taken from those 1,260 views. That’s less than 5%.

The problem is not the Google My Business platform; it’s that not nearly enough businesses take full advantage of its impressive features. And that’s why we’ve written this guide. Here, we’re going to share 13 optimization strategies:

Claim your Business Profile
Complete every section of your Google My Business account
Be meticulous with contact information
Select primary and secondary categories
Mark off applicable attributes
Write a complete “from the business” description
Publish Google posts weekly
Upload new photos weekly
Answer questions
Collect and respond to reviews
Add your products and/or services
Set up messaging
Maintain your Business Profile", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPbjl0RoaoGAGijW0E7QTyXhCjUdS3dRMGKLHk=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2022-10-12T12:00:25", "expires_at": "2023-04-13T12:00:25", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8918810828902568516", "text": "𝗗𝗼𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗼 𝗗𝗼𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀: 𝟭𝟬 𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝟮𝗗 𝗦𝘂𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀

With the ease of selling online, it’s easy to forget just how important human connection can be in sales.

TikTok marketing is the practice of using TikTok to promote a brand, product or service. It can include different tactics, like influencer marketing, TikTok advertising and creating organic viral content.

TikTok marketing can help businesses:

Increase brand awareness
Build engaged communities
Sell products and services
Get feedback from customers and audiences
Provide customer service
Advertise products and services to target audiences
Here are the three major types of marketing brands use on TikTok.

TikTok influencer marketing

TikTok influencer marketing is a big part of the app’s ecosystem. Mega-stars like Charli D’Amelio, Addison Rae, and Zach King can make a huge impact on the success of a business (tens of millions of users watch their content every day).

Big brands use emotion in their copy all the time.

Why?

Because emotion sells.

No matter what the product is, it's usually bought because of how the customer feels about the item, what it will do for them and how it will make them feel.

Customers then try to justify the purchase with logic. So, since emotions instigate sales, copy has to evoke emotions.

If a customer has a problem that needs solving or a desire for a particular item, they're going to feel a wide range emotions before, during and after a sale. I sounds crass, but business copy needs to leverage these emotions.

In addition, customers always remember the way a company makes them feel and emotion makes advertising campaigns more memorable. That increases brand awareness and loyalty.

TikTok marketing is the practice of using TikTok to promote a brand, product or service. It can include different tactics, like influencer marketing, TikTok advertising and creating organic viral content.

TikTok marketing can help businesses:

Increase brand awareness
Build engaged communities
Sell products and services
Get feedback from customers and audiences
Provide customer service
Advertise products and services to target audiences
Here are the three major types of marketing brands use on TikTok.

TikTok influencer marketing

TikTok influencer marketing is a big part of the app’s ecosystem. Mega-stars like Charli D’Amelio, Addison Rae, and Zach King can make a huge impact on the success of a business (tens of millions of users watch their content every day).

But you don’t need a high-profile influencer for successful marketing—try to discover rising stars, or influencers in your niche. For example, a small cosmetics brand based in Vancouver might search up the hashtag vancouve rmakeup and find influencers like Sarah McNabb.

Creating your own TikToks

This option gives you the most freedom. Create a Business TikTok account for your brand (keep scrolling for detailed step-by-step instructions) and start making your own organic content.

Big brands use emotion in their copy all the time.

Why?

Because emotion sells.

No matter what the product is, it's usually bought because of how the customer feels about the item, what it will do for them and how it will make them feel.

Customers then try to justify the purchase with logic. So, since emotions instigate sales, copy has to evoke emotions.

If a customer has a problem that needs solving or a desire for a particular item, they're going to feel a wide range emotions before, during and after a sale. I sounds crass, but business copy needs to leverage these emotions.

In addition, customers always remember the way a company makes them feel and emotion makes advertising campaigns more memorable. That increases brand awareness and loyalty.

Just think of the John Lewis ads at Christmas time which have become an event in itself. 

Take a look at the steps below to start using emotion in your communications:
1. Write down all the problems your product solves or the desires that it satisfies.
2. Attach a descriptive emotion to each problem.

4. Talk about the benefits of your product or service and how it will make your customers feel.

[{"id": "267314007842386192", "text": "How Tony Zhu of LC Signs Turned Viral Content Into Sales Growth

Tony Zhu of LC Signs transformed a traditional signage business into a global sensation using viral short-form video content. By blending humor, exaggerated accents, and relatable skits with clear product demos, he captured attention and built trust across social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram.

LC Signs’ viral campaigns not only entertained but drove real sales: followers engaged with videos, shared content, and submitted inquiries that converted into orders. Key strategies included balancing entertainment with product promotion, using audience interaction as co-creation, and leveraging trending audio, hashtags, and concise storytelling.

Short-form videos demonstrated products effectively, while engaging content encouraged followers to participate, boosting brand awareness and credibility. LC Signs now boasts hundreds of thousands of followers, millions of views, and increased sales inquiries directly from viral posts.

The lesson for businesses is clear: creative, consistent, and engaging content can turn social media virality into measurable growth.

Jungle Communications helps brands craft bold marketing campaigns and compelling content to drive engagement and revenue. Visual storytelling is a powerful way to connect with your audience using images, videos, infographics, and more. There are two main types: short-form and long-form.

Short-form storytelling delivers concise messages quickly. Think social media posts, short videos, reels, or ads. It’s great for building brand awareness, announcing updates, highlighting products, testing ideas, and encouraging engagement.

Long-form storytelling provides in-depth content over a longer period. This includes documentaries, comprehensive videos, or detailed visual sequences. Use it to educate, explain complex topics, cover multiple subjects, or keep audiences engaged longer.

Many brands benefit from combining both approaches. Short-form captures attention fast, while long-form deepens understanding and builds loyalty. Together, they create a well-rounded marketing strategy that reaches a broader audience.

At Jungle Communications, we help brands craft both short-term content and long-form visual stories to maximize engagement. From social media posts to comprehensive videos, we make your brand’s story memorable and impactful.

Google Search is evolving fast, and AI is now reshaping how people discover businesses online. Traditional “10 blue links” are gone — today’s results are visual, interactive, and personalized. Google’s AI (including AI Overviews/SGE) now understands context, summarizes answers at the top of the page, and analyzes images, voice, and video to deliver more accurate results.

For businesses, this means visibility depends on quality, helpful content — not keyword stuffing. To stay competitive, make sure your website loads quickly, is mobile-friendly, and uses structured data so Google can understand your pages. Optimize for voice and visual search by adding alt text, captions, and clear metadata for all images and videos.

Local search matters more than ever. With AI personalizing results based on location and behavior, keeping your Google Business Profile updated is essential. Ensure your NAP (name, address, phone) is consistent, upload high-quality photos, post weekly updates, and encourage customer reviews.

To stay ahead, create content that answers real customer questions, use AI tools to streamline workflows, and monitor performance through Google Search Console and Analytics. Most website visitors leave without buying about 96% and many never return on their own. Retargeting helps you win them back by showing targeted ads to people who already visited your site, viewed products, or abandoned their cart.

Retargeting works because it meets customers where they already are—on social media, search engines, mobile apps, and websites they browse daily. By reminding shoppers of what they viewed (or left behind), you increase the chances they come back and complete a purchase.

Retargeting can take many forms:
• Display ads that show products someone viewed
• Cart-recovery emails reminding shoppers what they left behind
• Search ads (RLSAs) tailored to past visitors
• Social ads targeting users who engaged with your posts or visited your page
• Mobile retargeting that reaches people on their phones

The key is personalization—showing the right message to the right person at the right time. Whether it’s highlighting a product they saw, offering a discount, or sharing social proof, retargeting boosts conversions and keeps your brand top of mind.

• Say “No” When Needed: You don’t have to attend every event or take on every request.
• Prioritize Self-Care: Rest, eat well, move your body, and recharge—your work will benefit.

Some decisions we make are not logical. Our subconscious receives stimuli and makes us make purchasing decisions. Knowing this, marketing has been using some mental triggers for years to succeed in campaigns.

We separate 6 mental triggers used in marketing and sales to show you:

. Urgency: short term to take action. (Ex: Buy TODAY!);

. Authority: whoever is speaking knows about the subject. (Ex: Use of certificates, seals and conversations about subjects in the area of ​​expertise);

. Scarcity: Product quantity or time limit. (Ex: giving the feeling that it will end and you will run out);

. Reciprocity: Offering an advantage in exchange for something. Often used for lead capture. (ex: Leave your email and win a complete ebook).

. New: You Know First! Everyone likes to feel important and special. (Ex: knowing or gaining information/product first);

. Social Proof: Those who bought it liked it and recommended it. (Ex: use of testimonials and reviews).

👉🏻 Good strategies make all the difference when choosing between buying from your brand or your competitor!

[{"id": "8945455706256905646", "text": "The person on the screen may not be the person you hire. ⚠️

Remote hiring has made it easier for fraudulent identities, fabricated credentials, and interview impersonation to move further into the hiring process before flags surface.

Remote hiring often spreads the steps across separate handoffs—recruiting, video interviews, background screening, equipment delivery, IT access, and payroll. A fraudulent candidate may appear credible at one checkpoint, while the inconsistency does not emerge until much later.

A recent New York State Bar Association analysis describes remote jobs as a particular target for fraud.

The risk is more than a bad hire; it can involve access to systems, sensitive information, and company equipment. 🔐

A stronger process does not mean slowing every hire down. It means being intentional.

Our customers may be impacted by a slower hiring process, but we must protect them from this new and increasingly common risk. 🛡️

We have built a process that’s working. We don’t post the details for a variety of reasons, but our CEO is happy to share information 1/1.

Message our CEO, Gina Herrera, directly through LinkedIn. 🤝

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPy1puLFxz5XPvF_R6qnfDWFmwEqeEvMqbQCXqC=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-17T16:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-15T14:51:19", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5400033977539034492", "text": "New York City added 64,000 private-sector jobs over the year through July, bringing total private employment to more than 4.2 million. 📈

The city’s unemployment rate was 5.0%, while New York State’s rate was 4.4%. Growth was strongest in education and health services, professional and business services, and financial activities. (NY DOL)

At the same time, city government continues to face a meaningful staffing gap, details noted in last month’s posts.

The takeaway for employers?

Qualified people continue to have options. 🎯

Whether candidates are considering private-sector roles, public service, or a career change, the hiring experience matters. Clear expectations, timely communication, and a thoughtful process help organizations hold attention. 🤝

Happy to share what we are seeing in the market, as we are close to all these hiring sectors.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOoXnrjre-5QmRvDz9bC43S8o7KgkhDqg-HlKBl=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-15T14:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-15T14:47:20", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5976502670920685393", "text": "The job description is a small part of the story. 📄

The day-to-day reality of a role is often where the best hiring decisions are made.

What does success look like in the first 90 days?

What are the internal relationships/departments they work with?

What is the supervisory structure?

How are shifts and schedules made?

At Expedient, our recruiters dig into those details before presenting candidates. 🔎

It drives better results and improves stickiness.

At Expedient, we have seen that the right match starts with a clearer understanding of the work. 🤝

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMb9xd0QVtrbMH3Uy4h58x75JOSIy_76DOeNMZI=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-02T14:27:52", "expires_at": "2027-03-04T14:27:51", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "691286172297350263", "text": "When you trust a partner with your contact center and onboarding, you’re really trusting their systems. 🤝

That’s one reason why we started on the journey of getting ISO certified. We are in the process of earning two ISO certifications: one focused on our contact center quality system and one on our onboarding/payroll processes, with both covering how we test AI, manage QA, and use scorecards to monitor performance. 

These ISO standards mean an independent assessor is verifying that we:

1️⃣ Have documented, repeatable processes for how calls are handled, monitored, and improved.

2️⃣ Run a structured quality management system (QMS) across our contact center so service is consistent, auditable, and compliant.

3️⃣ Apply the same rigor to onboarding and payroll, ensuring data accuracy, secure handling of worker information, and clean handoffs between systems.

The best part? The assessor noted that the foundation was already built and operating before we started the certification process! 

ISO is now formalizing and strengthening what the team had put in place over time.

Always so grateful for our tenured team! 👏

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNWXji-JRmBczpo3mW4RoozIg1AdavfU0_aT9fX=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-27T14:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-02-23T17:54:24", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2246343400424438846", "text": "HR and recruitment are on the minds of execs. 💭

The talking points continue to be “HR should be more strategic,” but now specifically, they’re asking for speed and adaptability—in hard numbers.

Deloitte’s 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report found about 70% of leaders now see speed and nimbleness as their primary competitive strategy for the next three years, yet only a small fraction (roughly 1 in 10) believe they’re making strong progress. (LinkedIn)

What that means:

Recruiting can’t be a slow, process-heavy, one-off event. You’ll need pipelines, solid sourcing platforms, strong candidate relationships that are nurtured, and partners who can flex skills and headcount quickly as work and priorities shift. 💪

These are all areas where Expedient plays a key role with our clients. 🤝

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPm0vlj-WEIzjrWGMAYz3TgDTpKQNv7lgTUNJHv=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-19T16:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-02-16T00:00:39", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8013870273201768459", "text": "A recent HR Dive article on contact center culture makes a powerful point: culture is not just a “nice to have”—it can deliver measurable ROI through lower attrition and better team performance. 📈

That’s especially relevant in environments where turnover is expensive, training is ongoing, and every new hire affects the customer experience. (HR Dive)

At Expedient, we didn’t start out with a specific focus on trying to build a certain culture—we just operated the way we knew would serve clients, candidates, and our teammates.

We focused on creating opportunities and arming people with skills. We did the right thing. And we worked hard to meet goals. 🤝

We hired and kept people who were in alignment.

Today, that is our unique culture—the Expedient Way. And it has held, even as we have moved to remote operations. 

When teams feel supported, they stay longer, perform better, and deliver a stronger experience for callers—which is exactly why culture belongs in the business case. 👥

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOKE5UfKLozYDIUEgYvNsjOzfExlQVuDXT-HZX7=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-18T14:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-02-15T23:57:19", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "342157093494263275", "text": "Contact center support! 📞

QA testing in contact centers: the difference between “working” and providing the highest levels of service.

If your contact center is using AI, QA testing is one of the best ways to make sure the technology is actually helping, not creating hidden problems. 

AI can speed up service, surface answers, and support agents, but only strong QA can confirm that the customer experience is still accurate, respectful, and compliant. ✅

For HR and ops leaders, this matters because the wrong response at scale becomes a very expensive mistake. 

Expedient uses QA to review outcomes, spot patterns, and improve the customer experience continuously.

We handle a high volume of calls and focus on how quickly we do it, but speed only counts if the caller leaves satisfied. 🤝

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipN7zkiV8q-9tho79eKfS0cpdPJ7P27Q2ZCtEOjS=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-11T14:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-02-08T22:29:54", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "863524116701817831", "text": "NYC by the numbers. 📊

1) NYC private-sector jobs are still growing.
Private-sector employment in New York City rose by about 53,400 jobs over the year, reaching roughly 4.26 million private jobs as of June 2026. 📈

2) Growth is concentrated.
Over the last year, the biggest gains were in private education and health services, professional and business services, and financial activities, with modest increases in information and construction. 🏙️

3) City government had a roughly 300,000-person workforce, with higher-than-normal vacancies.
NYC government has an authorized full-time headcount of about 305,589 roles for 2026, but as of the end of May the actual full-time headcount was 292,483, leaving a vacancy rate of about 4.3% (NYC Comptroller). 💼

4) The long hiring freeze has effectively eased.
The City previously operated under a “2-for-1” policy where many agencies could only fill one vacancy when two employees left. That restriction has now been lifted, and agencies can hire up to their personnel budgets. ✅

5) Government jobs are still a major part of NYC’s economy.
As of spring 2026, government employment in NYC stood at around 619,400 jobs, up from about 611,700 a year earlier, meaning public-sector roles are growing modestly. Yet many roles remain open! 🏛️

We hire for the City on a regular basis! Reach out to a recruiter today! 🤝

[{"id": "6897722178652202190", "text": "FischTank PR CEO Eric Fischgrund recently moderated a Heatmap News webinar entitled "The Climate & Energy Tech Investment Shift," sponsored by FischTank. [{"id": "469091227462645662", "text": "More views don't always mean more sales.

A campaign can generate impressive reach and engagement, yet have little impact on business growth.

The reason? Views measure attention—not customer intent.

The metrics that truly matter are:
✔ Conversions
✔ Click-through rate
✔ Purchases
✔ Revenue

A post with thousands of views but no customers isn't as valuable as one that consistently drives sales.

The most successful brands don't chase vanity metrics - they focus on results that grow the business.

👉 The next time your content performs well, ask yourself: How many people took action? That's the metric that drives real growth.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMa9XC2EyzLGCWfvW7Ya5bfkWPue1RVLj7ZwM8s=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://calendly.com/tiktokads-discovery/1-1", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-02T07:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-01-30T14:20:25", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1946469077901744686", "text": "Social media management is more than just posting content.

Posting every day is only one part of the process. Real social media management builds the foundation for long-term business growth.

It helps your brand create:
✔ Recognition that keeps you top of mind
✔ Clear positioning that sets you apart
✔ Trust that makes buying decisions easier
✔ A loyal community that advocates for your business
✔ Consistency that strengthens your brand over time
✔ Sustainable growth that turns attention into results

Content is the output. Strategy is what drives lasting success.

👉 Invest in a social media strategy that builds your brand, not just your posting schedule.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNGV5Moo7lJzdat-wkHJljs-2TpafiMRBJIVWsF=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://calendly.com/tiktokads-discovery/1-1", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-01T06:30:00", "expires_at": "2027-01-30T13:12:36", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "300595872040080945", "text": "Getting views is great. Being remembered is even better.

Many brands generate strong engagement, but few build lasting recognition.

The difference? Successful brands consistently reinforce:
✔ The same core message
✔ Clear positioning
✔ A recognizable visual identity
✔ A consistent point of view

Attention is temporary. Brand recognition creates long-term growth.

Here's a quick test:
If you removed your logo, username, and profile picture, would people still recognize your content?

If not, it's time to focus on building a memorable brand, not just creating content.

👉 Consistency turns attention into trust, and trust turns into growth.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMJtmEq2xg0MIQnh2x8dWBXHBts6I9g2pdaDHJy=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://calendly.com/tiktokads-discovery/1-1", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-07-24T06:30:00", "expires_at": "2027-01-20T20:08:00", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5805700904940442423", "text": "Stop collecting AI tools. Start building an AI workflow.

The most productive marketers aren't using every new AI app, they're using the right tools for the right tasks.

A simple AI workflow could look like this:

📚 Research - Turn documents into actionable insights.
🎙 Voiceovers - Create natural-sounding narration in minutes.
🎥 Video Creation - Generate videos and multilingual content faster.
📊 Presentations - Build polished decks from a single prompt.
🧠 Visuals - Transform complex ideas into clear diagrams and frameworks.

The goal isn't to have the biggest AI toolkit.

[{"id": "4453795627228264462", "text": "How Slow Page Load Times Affect User Experience and Conversions

Slow page load times can quickly drive visitors away, especially as users increasingly expect websites to provide fast and seamless access to information. In fact, 40% of users may leave a website if it takes more than three seconds to load, making page speed an important factor in website performance. Slow-loading pages can create a poor first impression, increase visitor frustration, and reduce the likelihood that users will continue browsing or return to the site. They can also contribute to higher bounce rates as visitors abandon pages before engaging with the available content. For businesses, this can lead to fewer completed purchases, form submissions, calls, and other valuable conversions. Improving page speed is therefore an important part of creating a positive user experience, maintaining engagement, and supporting stronger digital marketing performance.

Poor user experience (UX) design can significantly affect website engagement and increase exit rates when visitors struggle to find information or complete basic tasks. Confusing navigation, cluttered layouts, and non-responsive designs can create frustration and encourage users to leave a website prematurely. According to HubSpot, 73.1% of web designers identify non-responsive design as a leading reason visitors leave a website. Complex menu structures, unclear category labels, and the lack of an effective search function can make it even harder for users to navigate a site. Improving website navigation, simplifying page layouts, and ensuring mobile responsiveness can create a smoother user experience and help keep visitors engaged longer.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOQjFU_sL5ycZYGRW96jpBtVkhtJ6sYYnVhQV7Z=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/#__", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-18T13:47:06", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T13:47:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8261491451143582574", "text": "Key Channels That Drive an Inbound Marketing Strategy

Inbound marketing is more than a single tactic; it combines multiple channels that work together to attract, engage, and convert potential customers. Understanding how each channel contributes to the strategy can help businesses allocate their marketing budget and resources more effectively. Search engine optimization (SEO) is one of the most important inbound marketing channels because it helps businesses reach people actively searching for relevant information, products, or services. Strong SEO relies on relevant content, on-page optimization, link building, and technical improvements to build search visibility and authority. When these elements work together, SEO can create a steady source of qualified organic traffic and support long-term inbound marketing growth.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOuHCohpEPoURutQZKqbFAKqBLusqHc0bYPoYbI=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/#__", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-16T13:45:02", "expires_at": "2027-03-18T13:45:01", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1395246117969144940", "text": "How Video SEO Works

Video SEO is the process of optimizing video content to appear in YouTube search results as well as Google’s video and universal search results. Unlike traditional SEO, video optimization places greater emphasis on user behavior, including watch time, viewer engagement, click-through rates, and session activity, along with metadata and technical factors. YouTube primarily evaluates signals such as watch time, engagement, and how viewers continue using the platform after watching a video. Google, meanwhile, relies more heavily on video metadata, structured data, and crawlable content on the page where the video is embedded. Optimizing for both platforms gives businesses more opportunities to gain search visibility and reach their target audience.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOeGaJAg3PJrollVnhKC76NqmBWRXRqz_loXsq4=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/#__", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-14T16:01:47", "expires_at": "2027-03-16T16:01:46", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5464183996525893733", "text": "Why a Consistent Brand Voice Matters

Brand voice is the consistent personality, style, and perspective a company uses across its content and communications. It influences word choice, messaging, tone, and how a brand presents its values and expertise to its audience. While the tone may change depending on the platform or content format, the underlying brand voice should remain recognizable and consistent. For example, a company may use a more professional tone in a white paper while taking a conversational approach on social media without losing its core identity. A clearly defined brand voice helps businesses create more cohesive content across websites, social channels, email campaigns, and other marketing materials. Over time, this consistency makes a brand easier to recognize, strengthens credibility, and helps build lasting audience trust.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPyo3013fSng0pJBRqbAAxEtRgMVq61sqgGannQ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign=GMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nychttps://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign%3DGMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nyc", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-11T15:56:02", "expires_at": "2027-03-13T15:56:00", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7776691982594541047", "text": "How Trigger-Based Marketing Works

Trigger-based marketing is a strategy that automatically delivers personalized messages when a customer takes a specific action, such as visiting a webpage, clicking a link, submitting a form, or completing another measurable interaction. Rather than sending the same marketing message to an entire audience, businesses use real-time behavioral data to determine when and what type of communication should be delivered. These automated messages can be sent through email, SMS, digital advertising, push notifications, and other marketing channels. By responding to customer behavior, trigger-based marketing helps businesses provide more relevant and timely communication throughout the customer journey. The approach can be especially effective because messages are delivered when a person has already demonstrated interest in a product, service, or topic. When properly configured, trigger-based campaigns can improve engagement, strengthen personalization, and make marketing efforts more efficient.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMZrBq2QErAVr5rVgk51Iihw05se21yt4h6vW1g=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign=GMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nyc", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-10T07:31:55", "expires_at": "2027-03-12T07:31:54", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "4059103285394398218", "text": "How AI Overviews Are Changing Organic Search Visibility

Search traffic is not disappearing, but the number of clicks available from traditional organic results is changing as Google answers more questions directly within the search results page. As AI Overviews have expanded across Google Search, studies have reported a 42% decline in organic search clicks compared with pre-launch baselines. This shift represents more than a temporary seasonal fluctuation because it changes how users discover information and interact with search results. People are still searching, but many can now find answers without visiting the websites that traditionally ranked for those queries. As a result, achieving a high organic ranking alone may no longer guarantee the same level of visibility, traffic, or lead generation. The opportunity remains, but it has shifted toward earning visibility throughout the SERP, including the AI-powered search experiences that increasingly influence how users discover and evaluate businesses.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPqIikZRQ9lH3poOcVT8iBq7O6D_25hvL7Yqzz8=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign=GMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nyc", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-07T16:43:51", "expires_at": "2027-03-09T16:43:50", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6141464397427655889", "text": "On-Page SEO Best Practices for Higher Search Rankings

On-page SEO optimization improves search visibility by making a website easier for both users and search engines to understand and navigate. A strong SEO strategy includes a logical site architecture, SEO-friendly URLs, mobile-responsive design, and fast page loading speeds to enhance user experience and support better indexing. Optimizing meta titles, meta descriptions, and header tags with relevant keywords also helps search engines interpret page content while encouraging higher click-through rates from search results. Internal linking further strengthens site authority by connecting related pages, distributing ranking signals, using descriptive anchor text, and eliminating broken links that can negatively affect usability. By implementing these on-page SEO best practices, businesses can improve organic rankings, increase qualified website traffic, and create a stronger foundation for long-term search engine performance.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMKRxLY6zBjgzH0e6EdMn-jc81rsWCbhoAaoy0Z=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign=GMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nyc", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-04T18:21:07", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T18:21:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6460067706550919526", "text": "Why Businesses Are Using Video for Employee Training

Effective employee training should be engaging, consistent, and easy to scale across an organization. As businesses look for more efficient ways to educate their workforce, video has become one of the most reliable tools for delivering clear, repeatable training content. Companies in industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, technology, and professional services are increasingly investing in video production in Connecticut to create high-quality training materials that support onboarding, compliance, safety, and skill development. Video-based learning allows employees to access information at their own pace while ensuring every team member receives the same consistent instruction. By combining professional production with strategic training content, businesses can improve knowledge retention, streamline training processes, and support long-term workforce development.


", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPmisjZMYzN7A6js_YizHKUwCENAl6JA2jk5Ly_=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://mackmediagroup.com/newyork-digitalmarketingagency/?utm_campaign=GMB&utm_medium=digital_marketing_nyc", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-02T18:17:03", "expires_at": "2027-03-04T18:17:01", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5517729702812629773", "text": "Why Social Listening Matters in Modern Marketing

Online conversations have become one of the most valuable sources of customer insight, helping businesses understand audience sentiment, protect their reputation, and identify new growth opportunities. This is why understanding what social listening in marketing is has become increasingly important for organizations of all sizes. As customers share opinions across social media, forums, blogs, and review platforms, social listening has evolved into a core capability for every modern digital marketing agency. Businesses use these insights to improve customer experiences, strengthen brand reputation, refine marketing strategies, and guide product development with real-world feedback. The growing demand for these capabilities is reflected in the rapid expansion of the social listening market, as more brands invest in data-driven tools to stay connected with their audiences and make better business decisions.

So as the web3 world takes shape, our clients will be ready!", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOx4CI5TfFvpgSZvnObJmTwoz6zRVimuX3xX08T=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "http://refreshimmersive.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2022-07-19T17:52:33", "expires_at": "2023-01-18T17:52:32", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3941438174970739238", "text": "What if your "store" looked nothing like a store at all?
When it comes to virtual commerce or activations, brands have the ability to design spaces that evoke feelings, embrace cultures, and offer a unique experience. To help our clients visualize that, we created a 3D space inspired by the waves. It's a balance of abstract art and e-commerce function. We see it as our own little castle in the sand. And as with all of our spaces, the potential to house products, showcase videos, artwork, or NFTs, and connect visitors to immersive elements that could help bring them closer to your brand.

What can we build for you?", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPoxLaIG0gPg-O0NR23lL9iqI63egamsJoRP7ID=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "http://refreshimmersive.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2022-07-19T17:30:44", "expires_at": "2023-01-18T17:30:43", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7309768590556798115", "text": "Take a look inside our Virtual Shopping Experience for The Gathering Shops. Fully integrated with Shopify, customers are able to browse the immersive 360° space and seamlessly add items to their cart as they go. The experience is browser-based (webVR) so it's accessible via any desktop or mobile device.

The environment and products are fully rendered in 3D with the design loosely based on The Gathering Shops brick and mortar location at Bell Works. The popup shop design provides each brand with a space they can customize and call their own. This gives them a much larger presence than they would in a typical ", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMyhr0pRZTGUwb1fPYpaczqOtS4GaO98r4eCZZY=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://refreshadvertising.com/portfolio/gatheringshops/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2022-07-15T19:42:41", "expires_at": "2023-01-14T19:42:41", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5108493256274463824", "text": "There’s nothing sexy about a scientific white paper. 
So when global telecom testing company, Spirent Communications, wanted a cost-effective way to get industry pros to download theirs, we teamed up with our friends at Silver Style Pictures to create a quick series of trailers that would get people excited to invest their time.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNMWMeLaGxTrz_GsdBTaHBhtMWnOJ79gk35zW5F=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "http://www.refreshadvertising.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2019-07-16T21:14:51", "expires_at": "2020-01-15T21:14:51", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6568469781487691712", "text": "Car dealers are notorious for having some pretty uninspiring commercials and social content. But what if we could create a campaign that was creative, eye-catching, and for a reasonable budget? Something that put the dealer in a new light with high-level branding and quality. In this case, ads that featured a cool car going fast and loud instead of an in-your-face salesman and low-budget graphics. Someone out there would surely be game to change things for the better, right?

Well our friends at Tom’s Ford were ready to mix things up. They offered the keys to their beautiful Shelby GT350 with the only demand that we do something special. So we teamed up with the amazing crew at Silver Style Pictures to execute a concept that combined a beautiful beast of an automobile set against an iconic building, our Bell Works home. The end result was a collection of TV spots, social media content, and 360° videos that are sure to leave their mark on the dealer community and beyond.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPI0oP0E0Ah_859rwBaZPfDxRItvTTGGpNGkHx_=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://refreshadvertising.com/portfolio/toms-ford-shelby-campaign/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2019-07-16T21:11:09", "expires_at": "2020-01-15T21:11:09", "promo_code": null}]

In 2026, orthodontic practices need to optimize for three things:

SEO: ranking on Google
AEO: getting featured in AI answer results
GEO: being cited by AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini

The good news? You don't need a new website. You need smarter content.
Here's where to focus:

📄 Dedicated treatment pages — One page each for braces, Invisalign, early treatment, adult treatment, with your city included
❓ Built-in Q&A sections — Real questions as headings, clear answers underneath. AI loves this format.
📚 Deeper educational content — Articles like "Braces vs. Invisalign: How to Decide" build authority with both patients and AI
📋 A real FAQ hub — Collect the 30 most common questions your team hears and organize them by topic

FAQs used to be an afterthought. In 2026, they're one of your most valuable marketing assets.
The practices showing up in AI results aren't just optimized for Google — they're structured to be cited.
👇 Does your website have dedicated pages for each treatment you offer?", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPl-tm5YMo-f7pzCXqEOtuJtNQmLjWlbTK8QiW-=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://advancemedia.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-04T01:01:41", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T01:01:40", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2688827088498574795", "text": "In 2026, patients considering LASIK, SMILE, PRK, and ICL build a shortlist long before they ever “become a lead.” They do it through Google, AI-generated answers, Maps, TikTok, YouTube, reviews, and content that either calms their fears or quietly sends them to another center.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPN_VAhqxq3dw34rH6XUkl2AerRU9GV2VKFDJep=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://advancemedia.com/blog/the-hidden-funnel-how-patients-actually-choose-a-refractive-surgeon-in-2026/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-02T08:00:19", "expires_at": "2027-03-04T08:00:18", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7400591835633169774", "text": "Organic search traffic is falling. Here's what to do about it. 📉
AI is changing how people search. Instead of clicking through links, they're getting answers directly from Google summaries — no visit to your website required.
The numbers tell the story:

18 months ago: 2 pages crawled = 1 website visit
6 months ago: 6 pages crawled = 1 visit
Today: 18 pages crawled = 1 visit

90% of Google searches now end without a single click.
But local practices have an advantage. Here's where to focus:

⭐ Reviews — Google reviews first, then Yelp, Facebook, and RealSelf
🎥 Patient videos — Short stories (under 30 sec) show up in AI search results
📱 Social media — Instagram, Facebook & TikTok are your second website
▶️ YouTube — Doctor FAQs and trend videos get picked up by AI
💬 Forums — Reddit, Quora, and Facebook groups create digital word-of-mouth
🏆 Local awards & press releases — Yes, they still influence AI search

The sky isn't falling — but the strategy has to evolve.

Across every aesthetic vertical we work with — plastic surgery, med spas, dermatology, refractive surgery — the data is consistent:
Performance Max outperforms traditional search campaigns every time.

Here's why:

💰 Traditional search leads: ~$150 each, high intent

Yes, some P Max leads run warmer. But when your team knows how to nurture them, it becomes a simple numbers game — and the numbers favor P Max.

[{"id": "629182475969692221", "text": "You have about three seconds to answer the question every visitor is silently asking.

"Am I in the right place?"

Not three minutes. Not thirty seconds. Three seconds.

Barely enough time for the visitor to scan your hero headline and register your website layout, and to either stay or hit the back button.

Most local business websites fail at this level because they're designed around what the business wants to say rather than what the visitor needs to know. 

As such, even though the website is beautiful, nowhere in the first three seconds does it clearly answer: what do you do, who is it for, and why should I trust you over the next result?

At Blacksmith Agency, web design starts with that question and works backward. 

Every layout decision or page structure is built around reducing friction for the visitor and increasing the likelihood of a conversion.

Mobile-first, SEO-friendly, and fast are the baseline.

Converting the people who actually land on it is the point. 

And we get you that.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMuWF471OKZdPNnWHDw6OgAv6gf7o2E2SXZdp7x=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-06-01T15:01:48", "expires_at": "2026-12-01T15:01:46", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1371319062687187041", "text": "A social media post has a half-life of about 24 hours.

An SEO-optimised blog post earns traffic for years.

This isn't an argument against social media.

It's to help you see what each channel is best at, and how they complement one another.

Social media is built for real-time engagement, fast reach, and brand personality. This is what builds familiarity with people who do not need your products or services yet.

SEO is built for the future. It is good for capturing intent at the moment someone is ready to buy, building authority that compounds over time, and earning traffic that doesn't disappear when you stop posting.

Local businesses that grow consistently use both and connect them deliberately. 

The social content drives traffic to SEO-optimised pages. The SEO insights inform what social content to create. The website converts the visitors that both channels deliver.

At Blacksmith Agency, we manage all of it together (social, SEO, web design, PPC) as one strategy rather than four separate expenses.

The businesses that thrive online aren't doing more.

They're just doing it in the right order.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOo2NbL8_3SujTubj-1dj9eY2Zk0kJPcMANm_qC=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-29T15:02:35", "expires_at": "2026-11-28T15:02:33", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "4094600432656454551", "text": ""Should we do SEO or PPC?" is the wrong question any day.

Because neither one alone is the answer.

PPC gets you there fast. SEO keeps you there.

PPC without SEO means you're always one pause away from disappearing from the results page entirely.

SEO without PPC means playing a long game with no short-term wins, which is hard to explain to your internal team

Together, they cover each other's weaknesses. 

At Blacksmith Agency, we don't pitch SEO or PPC. We look at where a business is, where it wants to get to, and what combination of channels gets it there with the least waste.

In 2026, the businesses that dominate locally aren't the ones that chose the right channel.

They're the ones who stopped thinking in channels.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMkIilrTrUCxqZGfxfnFNdzNPhtvqii5RUfyA17=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-27T15:01:34", "expires_at": "2026-11-26T15:01:33", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "355905560373164917", "text": "People don't buy from businesses they find. They buy from businesses they recognise.

There's a difference, and it's where most local business marketing quietly falls apart.

Finding is easy. 

A Google search, an ad, a social post. But recognition is earned over time through consistency, with the same voice, visual identity, and message across every touchpoint. 

On the flip side, inconsistency erodes the trust that converts browsers into buyers.

At Blacksmith Agency, brand consistency is a strategy conversation we have with our clients.

We integrate web design, SEO, social media, and PPC so the message is coherent, and nothing is out of sync. Same positioning. Same tone. Same reason to choose you over everyone else.

A fragmented brand is a leaky bucket. You can keep filling it, or you can fix the holes.

We fix the holes.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPgMywYgbaLtjMnp--AdD6_diVmdt2175hYSSne=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-25T15:01:55", "expires_at": "2026-11-24T15:01:53", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5838908550248741566", "text": "Someone in your area searched for exactly what you offer today.

The question is whether they found you or your competitor.

That's what local SEO positions you for, yet it is the part of digital marketing that most local businesses underestimate.

The idea is simple. 

You need to make sure every signal Google uses to rank local businesses is consistently telling the same story about who you are, where you are, and what you do.

That includes your website structure, content, reviews, listings, and backlinks.

At Blacksmith Agency, local SEO sits at the centre of everything we build. 

It connects to the content we write, the PPC campaigns we run, and the websites we design.

And the goal? So that the right people in your area find you first

The customers are already searching.

The only question is who they're finding.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNX6CvEjVOV_ddgyr_fNbTw_fhNlh651z9gNMXS=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-22T15:02:02", "expires_at": "2026-11-21T15:02:00", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6070102076064434784", "text": "Vague marketing goals produce vague results.

"We want more visibility." 
"We want to grow our page online." 
"We want to increase engagement."

These aren't strategies; they are wishes. And wishes always sound great.

The local businesses that grow consistently go beyond mere wishes. They are specific with their targets and focus on what will actually drive revenue. 

At Blacksmith Agency, we start every client relationship by agreeing on what success actually looks like in measurable terms. 

Then we build the strategy around that and tailor our periodic reports towards the agreed metrics.

Measurable results isn't a promise.

It's what happens when you decide upfront what you're measuring. 

We can get that for you.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOBN9DCl5b1aS6Hb13nLOD2pBygyyAXMrTNWvXG=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-20T15:30:38", "expires_at": "2026-11-19T15:30:37", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3448549429068676381", "text": "Most local businesses don't have a marketing problem. They have a challenge with following through.

The website gets built and never gets updated.
Social media posts go out for a month, and then nothing happens for two.
An ad campaign launches, gets some traction, then nobody checks the numbers. 

Individually, none of it looks like failure. But together? It's why the phone isn't ringing as it should.

Marketing compounds when it's consistent. 

A website that's regularly updated helps SEO. 
SEO that is working makes PPC more efficient. 
PPC data that gets reviewed improves content. 
On-brand content strengthens social. 
An active social presence builds trust, which helps conversions. 

Each channel makes the others more effective, but only if someone is actually running them as a system.

That's what Blacksmith Agency does for local businesses. 

Instead of five separate services, we integrate web design, SEO, PPC, social, and content into one system and track them all so you can see what's working and cut what isn't.

Consistency isn't a personality trait. It's a process.

We build the process for you.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMSCqsn8Ye_iveT8At3B9DsYqT8u9N2u-ywvFQb=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-05-18T19:01:16", "expires_at": "2026-11-17T19:01:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3134836630973163413", "text": "The goal of PPC shouldn't be clicks.

It should be information.

Every ad campaign you run tells you something: which keywords convert, which messages resonate, which audiences are actually ready to buy. 

Most businesses collect that data and use it to run better ads. The smarter ones use the data to build an SEO strategy.

That's the shift. 

PPC gives you real-time proof of what works.

SEO takes that proof and compounds it, building organic rankings around the exact terms and intent your ads already confirmed are worth chasing.

[{"id": "551386440558563884", "text": "I don’t like the word “productivity”- Not that I don’t like being productive, I do. But I’d love to challenge the notion that productivity is some innate virtue.

As computers get faster and the economy more and more global, we are being asked to produce more and more to compete with machines, and workers in developing economies. And the value of that production is being stripped down by this rebalancing.

“It’s not enough to be busy; so are the ants. The question is: what are we busy about?” ~Henry David Thoreau

We’re not machines, or ants, we’re humans. We can’t endlessly produce… If you choose to be a creator/producer that’s great, but what if you just want to stare at the world and observe all day? I believe that also has value…

As artists and creatives we can’t just be doing-doing-doing all the time – there are only so many hours in the day and we need time to observe, participate and learn from the world around us", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNVX6eghoQxrVsOjglpql8AINy7PMcl3KQ2u0Hn=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://superbrand.la/being-productive-doesnt-mean-being-a-machine/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2020-09-30T23:42:00", "expires_at": "2021-04-01T23:42:00", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7595667830969997125", "text": "Creativity can only exist in a judgement free environment. As soon as judgement takes hold, particularly from our own mind, creativity is stifled.

Yesterday I was driving down a random street in LA and noticed the trees growing from little dirt patches dotting the sidewalk.

I thought to myself that a tree is the ultimate creative act. Every twist of its trunk, every outstretched limb is the product of a creative decision that, once made, defines how the tree will look and function as a whole.

If ever the tree looked around its urban environment and judged itself or its surroundings would it continue to grow? Would it continue to sprout limbs, branches, leaves or flowers in this foreign, unfriendly environment of concrete and steel?

If it asked, “Is this the right time?” or “Is this the right place for me to grow?” would it still move forward with life?

One of the reasons I’ve been able to be involved in so many incredible creative projects throughout my life is because I’ve always been able to put my own judgements aside.

I actually used to practice this when I was younger. I began at 19, a particularily difficult time in my life.

Whenever I’d sense my mind judging I’d practice diverting attention to something else. At the time it was a forest and a waterfall. I’d hold the picture of that forest in my mind for as long as it took for the judgements to die down (they always do). Then I’d continue on my way.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNqG2e3ShV6-qQGkQEUg2tIz1G9D09VhfBwMuG4=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://superbrand.la/10x-creativity/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2020-09-30T23:39:44", "expires_at": "2021-04-01T23:39:44", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1651906107845602611", "text": "I’ve had several conversations this week that have led to this post…

It seems several people I’ve spoken to recently mistakenly equate branding with visual identity.

The two are not interchangeable.

Branding is the entirety of your customer experience. Any contact you have with a client that is repeatable or consistent is a part of that experience.

Your logo and design is only a part of that experience. Good design is a huge value add but it’s not your branding, it’s your visual identity.

Visual identity is its own thing within the larger brand experience.

Don’t mistake good design for a strong brand. There’s plenty of great design out there representing weak brands and plenty of bad design representing strong brands.

The backbone of any strong brand is: 1) An ideal that resonates throughout the customer experience. 2) A customer experience that’s repeatable and consistent.

That’s it. You can go into the nitty gritty, of course, but it doesn’t have to be more complicated.

Stand for something then prove it by consistently creating an experience around it. That’s your brand.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMs-hCvavlAAVGAOeWOvY5_OMy-NzynFqXdTUW9=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://superbrand.la/visual-identity-and-branding/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2020-09-30T23:22:25", "expires_at": "2021-04-01T23:22:25", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6588824786485901450", "text": "We remain open. Check out our website for the latest information.", "type": null, "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": "https://superbrand.la/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2020-09-29T19:52:47", "expires_at": "2020-10-27T19:52:47", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2472352845705646863", "text": "We're open and here to help!", "type": null, "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2020-09-28T17:58:24", "expires_at": "2020-10-26T17:58:24", "promo_code": null}]

[{"id": "8260915006154675714", "text": "7 Web Design Trends for 2024
Here are the key trends that will define the future in web designing:

* Denser, Richer Graphics
Expect websites filled with complex textures, colors, and patterns. With better GPUs and faster processors, designers can create visually stunning, high-resolution graphics without sacrificing performance.

* AI-Generated Designs
AI is revolutionizing web design by generating custom graphics and layouts based on user preferences. This leads to more personalized user experiences and shorter design timelines.

* Skeuomorphism
Skeuomorphic designs, which mimic real-world objects, are making a comeback. This helps users navigate sites more intuitively by integrating familiar elements like switches and buttons.

* Parallax Scrolling
Parallax scrolling, where background and foreground content move at different speeds, will see a resurgence with added live content and videos for a more dynamic experience.

* Kinetic Typography
Animated text will become more interactive and responsive to user actions, making websites more engaging and visually appealing.

* Microinteractions
Subtle, personalized interactions like hover effects will improve user experience by guiding users through websites in a more intuitive way.

* Typography Evolution
Bold, experimental typography will take center stage, with creative fonts and layouts enhancing the overall design aesthetic.
Connect with our team at Red Millennial and discover how we can implement these trends for your brand", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNk-qoqm0uq1JxDcwaRrfOY42VN-5fwguBsD6J0=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://red-millennial.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2024-10-01T13:55:04", "expires_at": "2025-04-02T13:55:03", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8231941144281097852", "text": "People tend to judge businesses by their websites. Here's why you should spend on a reliable web designer.

Top 4 Benefits of Hiring a Professional Website Designer

1.	Improve the User Experience:
Even though your products or services may be industry-leading, you may not be able to attract potential customers if they have a bad experience using your website. Consequently, high bounce rates could hurt your search engine rankings. 

1.	Keep Up with Competitors:
Sometimes, it is about surviving in the market. At Red Millennial, the experts can design the websites so they work smoothly and your customers do not switch to competitors' websites. The designers will also help you generate leads and sales if you lag behind your competitors.

1.	Improve SEO Rankings:
A website that properly works and is user-friendly has a higher search engine ranking. Hence, your website has more chances to appear on the first page. Most people don't visit the second page, so you might obtain more audience and sales, especially if it is an e-commerce website.

1.	Engage Conversations:

[{"id": "9128945536912228780", "text": "🤖 How Do ChatGPT & Perplexity Choose Which Sources to Cite?

When a customer asks AI "who's the best divorce attorney near me?" the answer may decide who gets the call. There's no secret formula, but the pattern is clear: AI favors information that's relevant, verifiable, current, and clearly structured.

What actually earns a citation:

✅ Relevance over generic authority — a specific "emergency plumbing repair in Pasadena" page can beat a vague national article that's loosely on-topic
✅ Visible trust signals — who runs the business, where you operate, real experience, verifiable policies
✅ Freshness where it matters — outdated pricing or stale service pages become a liability on time-sensitive topics
✅ Clear structure — direct answers and descriptive headings beat walls of promotional copy
✅ Original proof — real pricing guides, case studies, and checklists beat recycled generic advice

One test before publishing: can this page answer a real customer question without making them work for it? "Best dentist LA affordable emergency dentist near me" helps no one — it's a shortcut, and AI tools recognize it as one.

AI citation isn't installed through tricks — it's earned by being the clearest, most credible answer when someone's deciding.

A mobile locksmith can be five minutes from a customer and still lose the Maps click to a competitor across town. The good news: you can absolutely build local visibility as a service-area business. Hiding your address doesn't mean removing location from the equation — Google still needs strong evidence of where you work and why customers trust you.

What actually helps:

✅ Set up your Google Business Profile as a service-area business — verify with your real operating address, hide it from public view, and list areas you genuinely serve
✅ Choose the most accurate primary category; keep hours, phone, and services complete and current
✅ Build real location relevance on your website — explain your service area in natural language, not repeated city names
✅ Earn honest reviews shortly after each job; respond with a real human voice
✅ Get accurate mentions on trade associations, chambers, and relevant local platforms

Avoid the shortcuts: a virtual office or unstaffed mailbox isn't a workaround — it can trigger a suspension. And claiming 15 service cities without the reviews or content to back it up won't fool customers or search engines.

The businesses that win make one promise easy to verify: we serve this area, we do this work well, and people here trust us.

A homeowner searches "emergency plumber near me" at 10:30pm. A patient asks AI which clinic accepts their insurance. Short answer: organic traffic isn't dying — easy, low-intent clicks are just harder to earn. And for small businesses, fewer high-intent visitors often beat a giant pile of random pageviews.

Why it feels harder: search results are crowded with ads, maps, AI summaries, and answer boxes. Simple questions get answered before someone even reaches your site. But zero-click search isn't zero-opportunity search — a person needing a licensed technician or comparing treatment options still needs a real business with availability, reviews, and proof of experience.

What actually moves the needle in 2026:

✅ Fix your highest-value service and location pages before publishing more blog content
✅ Keep business info accurate and consistent everywhere
✅ Build a repeatable process for earning recent reviews
✅ Answer real pre-sale questions — cost, timelines, comparisons
✅ Improve page speed, mobile usability, and lead tracking

SEO also compounds — unlike paid ads, it keeps working after you stop actively investing. The businesses gaining ground aren't chasing keyword volume. They're the clearest, most credible answer for their neighborhood.

A new website is like a storefront on a side street — it exists, but hardly anyone knows to walk in yet. For most small businesses, expect early movement in 3 to 6 months and more meaningful lead growth in 8 to 12 months. SEO isn't a light switch — it's closer to building a reputation.

What shapes your timeline:

✅ Starting point — an older site with technical issues may need cleanup first; a newer site needs time to build trust
✅ Competition — crowded categories like personal injury law or cosmetic dentistry take longer to break into
✅ Local signals — Google Business Profile accuracy, reviews, and proximity all influence map visibility
✅ Content quality over volume — a handful of strong, specific service pages beats 30 generic articles

A realistic path: Month 1 is research and fixes. Months 2–3 build relevance as key pages take shape. Months 4–6 bring early traction and refinement. Months 6–12 is where results compound — more pages rank, trust builds, and branded searches increase.

The fastest way to speed things up isn't shortcuts — it's fixing technical errors, keeping your business info accurate everywhere, and earning honest reviews consistently.

When a customer asks ChatGPT for the best local plumber or estate attorney, the AI isn't reading every page on the internet — it's looking for information it can quickly interpret, verify, and confidently use. That means your content needs to communicate in clean, self-contained sections AI can understand without guessing.

A few structural fixes that make a real difference:

✅ Lead with the answer, not the pitch — say exactly what the service includes and who it's for, before the brand language
✅ One idea per section — don't mix service timing, warranties, and pricing in the same paragraph
✅ Use clear headings — "What Happens During a Foundation Inspection?" beats "Peace of Mind Starts Here"
✅ Answer real questions — "How much does this cost?" and "Is this covered?" reflect how people actually ask AI tools
✅ Give direct answers real context — state the typical case, then name what changes it, instead of a vague "it depends"

AI systems are also cautious about unsupported claims. Show who's behind the information — credentials, experience, licenses, consistent contact details — and back claims with real evidence, not inflated promises.

Formatting alone won't build authority, but paired with genuine expertise, it makes your business easy to find and hard to ignore.

A visitor lands on your service page, reads two sentences, and leaves — not because you're the wrong fit, but because the next helpful page was nowhere in sight. Internal links (links from one page on your site to another) fix that, for both readers and Google.

Search engines use these links to discover pages and understand how your services, locations, and expertise relate to each other. Visitors use them to move from a question to a decision. Internal linking won't rescue thin content or a slow site, but it's one of the few upgrades that strengthens pages you already have — no ad budget required.

What good internal linking does:

✅ Signals to Google exactly what you do, where, and for whom
✅ Passes authority from high-traffic pages to the ones that drive revenue
✅ Gives readers a clear next step instead of a dead end
✅ Uses descriptive link text ("see our emergency plumbing services") instead of "click here"

Common mistakes to avoid: orphaned pages with no links pointing to them, linking everything back to just the homepage, and copy-paste location pages that all link to each other with nothing unique to offer.

Start with your revenue pages, then connect the content that naturally supports them.

A competitor posts new photos every week and suddenly seems to own the local map pack. Easy to connect the dots — but the real answer is more nuanced: yes, media and updates help, just not as a direct ranking button.

Google Maps rankings actually come down to three core factors:

✅ Relevance — how well your profile matches the search (accurate category, services, description)
✅ Distance — physical proximity to the searcher (no photo fixes this)
✅ Prominence — trust signals like reviews, citations, and site authority

Photos, videos, and posts mostly support relevance and prominence — they don't override weak categories, thin reviews, or inconsistent business info. There's no rule where a certain photo count guarantees a jump to the top.

That said, fresh, authentic media matters:

✅ Real photos of your team, storefront, and finished work build trust fast
✅ Short, honest videos reduce hesitation before someone calls
✅ Outdated visuals (or a 2019 exterior shot) create doubt at the worst moment
✅ Posts work best when specific — "Same-day water heater repair this week" beats "Great service"

Before chasing content, nail the fundamentals: accurate categories, consistent NAP info, a real review strategy, and strong location pages.

A $300/month offer sounds like a bargain — until six months pass and the phone still isn't ringing. A $5,000/month proposal can feel excessive if you're watching every expense. So what's realistic? For most U.S. small businesses, expect $750 to $3,000 per month, with competitive markets and bigger growth goals pushing that higher.

Common pricing formats in the U.S.:

✅ One-time audit — $750–$3,000 (identifies problems, doesn't include ongoing work)
✅ Local SEO retainer — $750–$2,500/month (Google Business Profile, local pages, reviews, citations)
✅ Broader SEO retainer — $2,000–$5,000/month (content, technical SEO, conversion, authority-building)
✅ Website SEO foundation project — $2,500–$15,000+ depending on site size and condition
✅ Hourly consulting — roughly $100–$250/hour

What drives the price: your market's competition, how many locations you have, your site's current condition, and what's actually included. Watch for red flags — guaranteed rankings, vague deliverables, mass-produced content, or sketchy backlinks. Cleaning up bad SEO often costs more than doing it right the first time.

The real question isn't the price tag — it's whether the work is designed to bring in qualified calls, bookings, and revenue.

These two page types get treated as interchangeable, but they solve different problems — and mixing them up can mislead customers.

A location page is for a real, staffed place customers can visit — an office, store, clinic, or showroom. It should answer: where is it, when is it open, can I walk in, is there parking? Strong ones include full address, hours, directions, branch-specific services, and real photos of the space.

A service area page is for markets you serve without a local office — think a plumber covering several cities or a mobile groomer visiting specific neighborhoods. These pages should explain coverage, dispatch times, and booking details — never imply there's a branch to visit.

The line matters: never present a mailing address, virtual office, or unstaffed suite as a customer-facing location. That erodes trust fast.

A simple test before building either: Does the business have a real, staffed presence there? Could a customer visit and not feel misled? If not, it's a service area page — not a location page.

Build separate city pages only when there's a genuine local difference — coverage, proof, or availability. Otherwise, one strong regional page beats five thin, repetitive ones.

[{"id": "7329842827137778381", "text": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x_8iMEviViY%5D(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v%3Dx_8iMEviViY", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fIO6y_SJw-k", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-21T22:39:49", "expires_at": "2027-03-23T22:39:49", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5147039997625105500", "text": ""I don’t trust producers."

That’s how a well-known director kicked off a shoot with me.

He had every right to be defensive—he’d been burned before by budget notes disguised as creative feedback.

Here’s a look at Challenge ", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOXrjnFxPEzma2AkTEcmmy4wRrBVQDh1DqvmLZI=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://youtu.be/dW3iYa23N3s?si=16z1JHK7-VbvkSkq", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-25T19:58:40", "expires_at": "2027-02-24T19:58:39", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "9135953569178951481", "text": "Blend recently teamed up with DIVE Studios, Intertrend, and Toyota Motor North America to produce "QUEST"—a 25-minute branded challenge series shot across Los Angeles featuring three custom Toyota RAV4 trims.

From format development and game design to multi-cam field production, our team brought this hostless challenge show to life.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOUQaSuvQHePlC4Ua6usHP8L5EH3-3-1b0qkjdC=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://youtu.be/vmITzGd11DE?si=CrMZpoQZudxpMvIO%5D(https://youtu.be/vmITzGd11DE?si%3DCrMZpoQZudxpMvIO", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-17T18:16:29", "expires_at": "2027-02-16T18:16:27", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5319187627172792431", "text": "True Alignment Over Negotiation

If everyone is winning in different ways, you’re not aligned. You’re negotiating.
The brand, the agency, and the production company all say they want the exact same thing: great work, a strong outcome, and a successful campaign. 

Yet, they rarely measure success the same way:
* Brands look to protect the overall business.
* Agencies focus on protecting the client relationship.
* Production houses work to protect creative execution.

When these priorities pull in opposite directions, the creative itself gets negotiated away. Decisions slow down, safe choices become the default, and endless feedback loops stall momentum.

The Operator Solution
The fix is simple: establish one core operator in the center who owns the outcome across all three fronts. Someone who can accurately translate, decide, and align how everyone wins together.
When you establish unified alignment, the best creative outcome naturally serves the business, strengthens the relationship, and holds execution to the highest standard. That's when projects move fast, and that’s when the work gets better.
Stop negotiating your creative. Align your production.
